analysis:
Examined both workflow changes, the complete supplied BASE/HEAD composite action, and unchanged file modes. .github/actions/provider-release-build/action.yml:354-367 adds a release-only binary compatibility check after building the CLI, enclave, fan helper and cluster helpers. Paths are quoted, and set -euo pipefail propagates checker failure. Existing source verification, lane separation, qualification and source-matched Metal checks remain unchanged. Cache saving can still run after a failed check (385-397), but the compatibility check is not conditional on a cache miss, so cache reuse does not visibly bypass it. .github/workflows/ci.yml:151-155 adds checker tests and a source comparison scan without removing existing checks.
These additions concern serving availability (A-018), signed-artifact qualification (A-017/T-054), and helper availability (TB-010); no supported regression is visible. They do not themselves alter authorization, attestation, request encryption, plaintext handling, cache isolation/TTL (T-041), billing or installer trust. No material threat-model expansion is established by the invocation changes alone.
Integration must inspect scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py, scripts/check-date-comparisons.py and their tests to establish parsing, fail-closed behavior and intended symbol/source coverage. Those implementations are absent here, so the new safeguards' effectiveness remains unverified, not evidence of a vulnerability. CI surrounding job configuration and downstream artifact publication were not supplied; this review does not establish end-to-end release enforcement.
